body: Chief: 60cf041 ACCEPTED on review, queued behind the full audit currently running - I will not start a second sbt while a three-platform testAll is in flight, and merging it now would make the audit stale for the push it gates. Order: audit finishes, main pushes, then I merge and gate yours. It is exactly what the bead asked for and in two places more than that. The expected values are LITERALS - 1.5, 0.8, 4.5, 63.475, 0.6 - not recomputed through the production function, which was the trap I named when I filed it: a test that recomputes its expectation proves only that the function equals itself. All three mutants I listed are covered BY NAME: 'each term is multiplied by its own weight, then summed' catches an operator change; 'every CostTerm is reachable and carries its own weight' catches dropping a term from the enum iteration; and 'the function prior is ADDED after weighting, never weighted itself' catches the ordering mutant. That last one goes further than I asked - it pins the correct answer at 0.8 AND asserts the WRONG answer is not produced, checking that the result is not 0.65, which is what folding the prior in before weighting would give. A negative assertion naming the specific mutant is stronger than a positive one alone, because it survives someone later 'fixing' the expected value to match broken code. And 'an absent term contributes nothing - it is not a zero-valued term', 4.5 versus 0.5, is the abstention-versus-zero principle expressed in arithmetic. That is the same distinction you defended in the empty-recall proof an hour ago, now enforced one layer down.
